Decisions" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="36" width="1700" x="40" y="8" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-2" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=13;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Goal:</b> keep the decision "where should this go?" right next to the truth of "who can take it now?" &nbsp;|&nbsp; <b>Rule:</b> optimize the USER's latency, not the balancer's bookkeeping; every layer exists because the one before it was not enough &nbsp;|&nbsp; <b>Example:</b> IPO allotment day = 40× normal traffic across 80+ microservices" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="44" width="1880" x="40" y="48" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-3" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;dashed=1;dashPattern=8 4;strokeColor=#b26a00;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingTop=4;fontStyle=1;fontSize=14;fontColor=#b26a00;" value="A · WHY — what problem is a load balancer really solving?" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="200" width="1910" x="20" y="100" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-4" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;dashed=1;dashPattern=8 4;strokeColor=#1a56a0;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingTop=4;fontStyle=1;fontSize=14;fontColor=#1a56a0;" value="B · EDGE &amp; HIGH AVAILABILITY — who gets the connection" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="370" width="1910" x="20" y="320" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-5" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;dashed=1;dashPattern=8 4;strokeColor=#2e7d32;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingTop=4;fontStyle=1;fontSize=14;fontColor=#2e7d32;" value="C · INSIDE THE LOAD BALANCER — the per-request decision pipeline" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="365" width="1910" x="20" y="710" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-6" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;dashed=1;dashPattern=8 4;strokeColor=#9673a6;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingTop=4;fontStyle=1;fontSize=14;fontColor=#9673a6;" value="D · HEALTH, DRAINING &amp; CONTROL — keep the server pool truthful" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="430" width="1910" x="20" y="1095" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-7" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Without a balancer:</b> every client guesses a server. 1,000 clients all pick Server A → A drowns, B sits idle. Capacity lives on the servers, the decision lives on the clients — they drift apart." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="140" width="430" x="40" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-8" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Decision 1:</b> keep the decision NEXT TO the truth of who can take traffic — in ONE place: the load balancer." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="140" width="430" x="520" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-9" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Decision 2:</b> optimize the USER's latency, not fairness. Equal request counts serve the balancer's bookkeeping; a request only cares how fast IT comes back." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="140" width="430" x="1000" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-10" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#666666;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>So naive round-robin fails:</b> it counts requests, not work. A 5 ms status check and a 2 s redemption look identical — three slow ones land on one server while its neighbour idles." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="140" width="430" x="1480" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-11" edge="1" parent="1" source="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-7" value="<b>Decision:</b> clients get ONE address and never pick a server. <i>Why:</i> thousands of clients guessing alone cannot know what the others chose." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="200" x="40" y="525" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-27" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Decision:</b> choose the REGION at DNS, before the connection opens. <i>Why:</i> distance dominates latency (~5 ms local vs ~25 ms cross-city, on EVERY request). <i>Alt:</i> round-robin across data centres." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="200" x="300" y="525" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-28" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Decision:</b> several ACTIVE LBs spread by DNS / ECMP. <i>Why:</i> one active LB hits its CPU / NIC ceiling on IPO day. <i>Trade-off:</i> coarse balance at DNS, precise decisions underneath." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="200" x="560" y="525" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-29" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Decision:</b> active + standby share a virtual IP (VRRP). <i>Why:</i> the LB is itself a single point of failure. <i>Cost:</i> a few seconds of failover — bounded. <i>Rule:</i> only the node holding the lease may own the VIP, so two active nodes can never exist (no split-brain)." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="470" x="870" y="525" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-30" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Trade-off:</b> a DR region means paying for capacity that mostly idles. <i>Why still:</i> losing a region without it is an outage for everyone. GSLB picks a REGION, the regional LB picks a SERVER — two different problems, two different speeds." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="490" x="1420" y="525" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-31" parent="1" value="<b>Shed gate</b><br>too much traffic? reject some fast" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="110" width="195" x="40" y="745" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-32" </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-43" parent="1" value="<b>Decision:</b> when ALL servers are drowning, reject some requests fast. <i>Why:</i> "least loaded" would pick the 128% server and degrade everyone. <i>Trade-off:</i> some users get "try again", not a slow timeout." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="175" width="195" x="40" y="870" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-44" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Decision:</b> L4 by default, L7 only where the path matters. <i>Why:</i> L4 is fast because it is blind; L7 can send /insurance to its own pool but costs CPU. Pay per route, not everywhere." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="175" width="195" x="280" y="870" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-45" parent="1" Neither alone is honest." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="916" x="40" y="1305" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-64" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Decision:</b> "healthy" is a vantage point, not a fact — a standby can see a server as dead while the active sees it as fine. Exactly ONE LB's opinion is acted on at a time. <i>Why:</i> two nodes routing under one identity is a correctness bug, not a health disagreement." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="916" </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-73" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Decision:</b> drain with a hard ceiling. <i>Why:</i> a hard kill cuts a real redemption mid-flight (user and ledger now disagree); waiting forever means a deploy that never ends. <i>Trade-off:</i> break the fewest requests, on purpose, with a bound." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="910" x="1000" y="1305" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-74" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Control plane</b> — pools, routes, weights, shed threshold, drain timeout. Changed through reviewed config, never by hand on a live LB." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="440" x="1000" y="1410" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-75" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Observability</b> — per-server latency · errors · connections · sheds · health flips. Debuggable at 3 a.m." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="440" x="1470" y="1410" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-76" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=16;fontColor=#222222;fontStyle=1;spacing=4;" value="How to read it — follow the numbers" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="900" x="40" y="1545" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-77" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Flow (①–⑫ and drain)</b><br>① A client asks for one address; GSLB (DNS) returns the nearest healthy region.<br>② Inside the region, DNS / ECMP spreads clients across several active LB pairs.<br>③ Each pair has an ACTIVE LB owning a virtual IP; a STANDBY watches its heartbeat.<br>④ Every request enters the decision pipeline.<br>⑤ Shed gate: truly overloaded? reject some fast. ⑥ Route: L4 by default, L7 reads the path to find the right pool.<br>⑦ Only healthy, non-draining servers are candidates. ⑧ Pinned session? send it home.<br>⑨ Pick the best server by live latency + connections. ⑩ Forward, and record how it went.<br>⑪ Active + passive checks update the health state. ⑫ That state feeds the filter at ⑦.<br><b>Drain:</b> a deploy stops NEW requests, lets old ones finish, force-closes stragglers after a ceiling.<br><br><b>Example:</b> IPO day, 40× traffic → GSLB → Chennai → one of several LB pairs → L7 sends /ipo/* to the IPO pool → shed gate protects the pool when all servers pass 100% → a mid-day deploy drains a server instead of killing live redemptions." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="480" width="610" x="40" y="1585" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-78" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Architect decisions — say "why A over B"</b><br>1. One place for capacity AND decision, not clients guessing.<br>2. Latency over fairness — the user feels speed, not equal counts.<br>3. Live-state algorithm over round-robin: count ≠ work, and connection count is a proxy, not load.<br>4. Health is its own signal; active + passive layered, each covering the other's blind spot.<br>5. L4 by default, L7 only where the path matters — paid per route.<br>6. Stickiness is a patch → move session state to a shared store.<br>7. The LB is a single point of failure → active + standby with a VIP; then scale out with DNS / ECMP.<br>8. "Healthy" is a vantage point → one LB's opinion acted on, a lease prevents split-brain.<br>9. Remove servers by draining, with a hard timeout.<br>10. Under true overload, shed fast instead of degrading everyone.<br>11. Geography changes the SHAPE of the problem → GSLB picks a region, the LB picks a server." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="480" width="610" x="670" y="1585" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pXfFpFgfbPjzgF4fko3J-79" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Mental model &amp; interview close</b><br><i>Problem → Constraint → Trade-off → Decision → New problem</i><br>decision + capacity together → latency → live state → health → high availability → scale-out → overload → geography<br><br><b>Trade-offs we accept</b><br>• Latency-aware routing → more state to compute<br>• L7 → CPU cost for reading every request<br>• Health checks → probe cost + blind spots<br>• Standby LB + DR region → idle capacity, a few seconds of failover<br>• DNS spread → coarse imbalance on top<br>• Load shedding → some users rejected on purpose<br>• Drain ceiling → a few stragglers cut<br><br><b>One-line close:</b> "A load balancer keeps 'where should this go?' close to 'who can take it right now?' — and every box in it exists because the box before it was not enough."<br><br><b>Honest test:</b> every backend at 130% — does it send everyone to the "least bad" server? It must not: it sheds fast and protects the pools.<br><br><b>Extend later:</b> TLS termination · per-client rate limiting · consistent hashing · canary routing · service-mesh sidecars." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="480" width="630" x="1300" y="1585" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div: C · INSIDE THE LOAD BALANCER — the per-request decision pipeline

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1896px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1098px; margin-left: 14px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #9673a6;

div.div: D · HEALTH, DRAINING & CONTROL — keep the server pool truthful

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(248, 206, 204), rgb(81, 45, 43)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(184, 84, 80), rgb(215, 129, 126));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 412px; height: 1px; padding-top: 202px; margin-left: 30px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Without a balancer: every client guesses a server. 1,000 clients all pick Server A → A drowns, B sits idle. Capacity lives on the servers, the decision lives on the clients — they drift apart.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 412px; height: 1px; padding-top: 202px; margin-left: 510px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Decision 1: keep the decision NEXT TO the truth of who can take traffic — in ONE place: the load balancer.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 412px; height: 1px; padding-top: 202px; margin-left: 990px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Decision 2: optimize the USER's latency, not fairness. Equal request counts serve the balancer's bookkeeping; a request only cares how fast IT comes back.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 412px; height: 1px; padding-top: 202px; margin-left: 1470px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: So naive round-robin fails: it counts requests, not work. A 5 ms status check and a 2 s redemption look identical — three slow ones land on one server while its neighbour idles.

div.div: Decision: clients get ONE address and never pick a server. Why: thousands of clients guessing alone cannot know what the others chose.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 182px; height: 1px; padding-top: 592px; margin-left: 290px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Decision: choose the REGION at DNS, before the connection opens. Why: distance dominates latency (~5 ms local vs ~25 ms cross-city, on EVERY request). Alt: round-robin across data centres.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 182px; height: 1px; padding-top: 592px; margin-left: 550px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Decision: several ACTIVE LBs spread by DNS / ECMP. Why: one active LB hits its CPU / NIC ceiling on IPO day. Trade-off: coarse balance at DNS, precise decisions underneath.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 452px; height: 1px; padding-top: 592px; margin-left: 860px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Decision: active + standby share a virtual IP (VRRP). Why: the LB is itself a single point of failure. Cost: a few seconds of failover — bounded. Rule: only the node holding the lease may own the VIP, so two active nodes can never exist (no split-brain).

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 472px; height: 1px; padding-top: 592px; margin-left: 1410px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Trade-off: a DR region means paying for capacity that mostly idles. Why still: losing a region without it is an outage for everyone. GSLB picks a REGION, the regional LB picks a SERVER — two different problems, two different speeds.

div.div: Decision: L4 by default, L7 only where the path matters. Why: L4 is fast because it is blind; L7 can send /insurance to its own pool but costs CPU. Pay per route, not everywhere.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.div: Decision: health is a SEPARATE signal from load. Why: a dead server shows 0 connections and looks like the BEST choice.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 177px; height: 1px; padding-top: 950px; margin-left: 750px;

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.div: Decision: latency-aware, not round-robin. Why: round-robin counts requests, not work; connection count alone can lie (11 slow calls vs 42 idle ones). Cost: more state to track.

Active checks
LB pings each server every few seconds. Cost = server count, not traffic (200 servers / 2 s = 100 pings/s, even at 3 a.m.). Blind spot: a shallow ping passes while a dependency is broken.

div.div: Decision: use BOTH checks — active for baseline liveness at low frequency (bounded cost), passive for fast reaction under real traffic. Why: health is an ESTIMATE from two signals; each one covers the other's blind spot. Neither alone is honest.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.div: Decision: "healthy" is a vantage point, not a fact — a standby can see a server as dead while the active sees it as fine. Exactly ONE LB's opinion is acted on at a time. Why: two nodes routing under one identity is a correctness bug, not a health disagreement.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 592px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1817px; margin-left: 30px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;

div.div:
Flow (①–⑫ and drain)
① A client asks for one address; GSLB (DNS) returns the nearest healthy region.
② Inside the region, DNS / ECMP spreads clients across several active LB pairs.
③ Each pair has an ACTIVE LB owning a virtual IP; a STANDBY watches its heartbeat.
④ Every request enters the decision pipeline.
⑤ Shed gate: truly overloaded? reject some fast. ⑥ Route: L4 by default, L7 reads the path to find the right pool.
⑦ Only healthy, non-draining servers are candidates. ⑧ Pinned session? send it home.
⑨ Pick the best server by live latency + connections. ⑩ Forward, and record how it went.
⑪ Active + passive checks update the health state. ⑫ That state feeds the filter at ⑦.
Drain: a deploy stops NEW requests, lets old ones finish, force-closes stragglers after a ceiling.
Example: IPO day, 40× traffic → GSLB → Chennai → one of several LB pairs → L7 sends /ipo/* to the IPO pool → shed gate protects the pool when all servers pass 100% → a mid-day deploy drains a server instead of killing live redemptions.

div.div:
Architect decisions — say "why A over B"
1. One place for capacity AND decision, not clients guessing.
2. Latency over fairness — the user feels speed, not equal counts.
3. Live-state algorithm over round-robin: count ≠ work, and connection count is a proxy, not load.
4. Health is its own signal; active + passive layered, each covering the other's blind spot.
5. L4 by default, L7 only where the path matters — paid per route.
6. Stickiness is a patch → move session state to a shared store.
7. The LB is a single point of failure → active + standby with a VIP; then scale out with DNS / ECMP.
8. "Healthy" is a vantage point → one LB's opinion acted on, a lease prevents split-brain.
9. Remove servers by draining, with a hard timeout.
10. Under true overload, shed fast instead of degrading everyone.
11. Geography changes the SHAPE of the problem → GSLB picks a region, the LB picks a server.

div.div:
Mental model & interview close
Problem → Constraint → Trade-off → Decision → New problem
decision + capacity together → latency → live state → health → high availability → scale-out → overload → geography
Trade-offs we accept
• Latency-aware routing → more state to compute
• L7 → CPU cost for reading every request
• Health checks → probe cost + blind spots
• Standby LB + DR region → idle capacity, a few seconds of failover
• DNS spread → coarse imbalance on top
• Load shedding → some users rejected on purpose
• Drain ceiling → a few stragglers cut
One-line close: "A load balancer keeps 'where should this go?' close to 'who can take it right now?' — and every box in it exists because the box before it was not enough."
Honest test: every backend at 130% — does it send everyone to the "least bad" server? It must not: it sheds fast and protects the pools.
Extend later: TLS termination · per-client rate limiting · consistent hashing · canary routing · service-mesh sidecars.
